text: More about active play with pawns
zh: 进一步谈兵的积极行动

text: The pawn wedge and the reaction to it. The pawn nail. The phalanx of e- and f-pawns. Pawn storm.
zh: 兵楔及其应对。钉子兵。e兵与f兵组成的兵阵。兵潮。

text: And so we have convinced ourselves that the role of the pawn in no way amounts to positional pressure, the control of squares of a certain colour, securing a handy base for piece forces; the pawns are also a powerful 1 means of attack. Without active pawn support, a piece attack often turns out to be doomed to failure, running up against a defensive bristle of enemy pawns. Consequently, one of the main attacking tasks of pawns is the removal of the opponent's defensive pawn line in the sector serving as an object of a planned attack. If, however, such a pawn attack is launched against castling, then it often leads to the creation of direct mating threats to the exposed king.
zh: 因此，我们确信兵的作用绝不等于位置压力，控制某种颜色的格，为棋子部队提供方便的基地；兵也是一种强大的1攻击手段。如果没有积极的兵支持，棋子的攻击往往注定会失败，因为会遇到敌人兵的防守。因此，兵的主要攻击任务之一是移除作为计划攻击目标的扇区中对手的防御兵线。然而，如果针对易位发起这样的兵攻击，那么通常会导致对暴露的王直接创建将杀威胁。

text: In practice, with active pawn operations, well known is the formation in the centre bearing the graphic name pawn wedge. The scheme of "driving" such a wedge appears in the following form.
zh: 实际上，在活跃的兵操作中，众所周知的是中心的编队带有图形名称兵楔。“驱动”这种楔子的方案以下列形式出现。

text: It should be noted that the formation e4-d5-c4 (for Black e5d4-c5) is called a wedge in the case when one of the opponent's pawns, adjacent to the wedging pawns, is still on its original square c7 or e7 (c2 or e2). Such a wedge is more dynamic (prospects of advancing c4-c5 or e4-e5 for White, correspondingly ... c5-c4 or ... e5e4 for Black), but in return less stable in view of the possibility of undermining it by the moves ...
zh: 应该注意的是，当与楔形兵相邻的对手的兵之一仍处于其原始格时，阵型e4-d5-c4（对于黑e5d4-c5）被称为楔形。c7 或 e7（c2 或 e2）。这样的楔子更具动态性（白方前进c4-c5或e4-e5的前景，相应地。。。c5-c4或。。。e5e4黑方），但鉴于移动可能破坏它的可能性，回报不太稳定。。。

text: c7-c6 or ... e7-e6 (c2-c3 or e2-e3).
zh: c7-c6 or ... e7-e6 (c2-c3 or e2-e3).

text: The undermining advance of the f-pawn serves as the basic method of struggle against the wedge. A careful assessment of the position will determine whether the construction of the wedge is favourable or unfavourable. The wedge, of course, allows the gain of space and cramps the opponent, but at the same time limits the dynamic resources and, uo the contrary, increases them for the enemy due to clear prospects of a lively pawn action on the king's flank. It is hardly worthwhile constructing a wedge just to somewhat cramp the opponent. The construction of a wedge is justified only in that case when it is possible to count on retaining the initiative or at least where there is the possibility of preventing the advance of the enemy f-pawn.
zh: 破坏冲兵是对抗楔子的基本方法。仔细评估位置将决定楔形结构是有利还是不利。当然，楔形允许获得空间并限制对手，但同时限制了动态资源，相反，由于在王翼上进行活跃的兵行动的明确前景，增加了敌人的动态资源。仅仅为了稍微限制对手而构建楔子是不值得的。只有在可以指望保留主动权或至少有可能阻止敌人f-兵前进的情况下，建造楔子才是合理的。

text: White more often has recourse to a pawn wedge than Black. In several ideological variations of the King's Indian Defence or Spanish Game, it is a logical link in the plan of play.
zh: 白方比黑方更常使用兵楔。在老印度防御或西班牙开局的几个意识形态变体中，它是对局计划中的逻辑链接。

The wedge ought to cramp Black, but here the basic motive of the cramping restriction of the activity of the king's bishop - is absent. Moreover, with the move d5 White actually limits the sphere of action of the king's bishop, only not the enemy's but his own. He should continue 8 e3 exd4 9 Nxd4 Nxd4
zh: 这种楔形入侵在这里没有什么基础。如果白方后来成功地通过下棋e4和f4在中间开始轻率推进，那么这可能有一定的道理。楔子应该限制黑方，但这里并没有限制王的象活动的基本动机。而且，白方d5实际上限制了王的象的行动范围，不仅不是敌人的，而是自己的。他应该继续 8 e3 exd4 9 Nxd4 Nxd4

text: On the board are opposite coloured bishops. In the endgame this often serves to guarantee a draw even when t the opponent has a considerable e material advantage. On the other hand, in the middlegame the presence of opposite coloured bishops quite often makes it easier for the attacking side to achieve victory. Usually this depends on the arrangement of the pawn chain. In the present game, the principal group of Black pawns extends over four squares - f6-e5d4-c5 (the wedge!). Meanwhile, he has a black-squared bishop which comes up against a barrier everywhere, in the shape of its own pawns. Another matter is the opponent's bishop, centering fire on the white squares which are the most important main lines on the board. If we add to this the fact that Black has a weak pawn on f6, his king is insecurely placed, its last cover - the h7 point - exposed to attack, and the enemy rooks dominate the weak white squares in the region of the king's flank, then it becomes clear that White has achieved a decisive advantage.

text: King's Indian Defence

text: This is a long-standing way of playing against the King's Indian Defence for White, and has recently become more and more frequently met in practice. It is wellknown that in his return match with Smyslov, Botvinnik likewise stuck to this treatment of the opening. The apparently very modest move of the f-pawn has great planning significance. It extends far beyond the limits of a simple striving to reinforce one of the main links of the pawn centre - the e4 pawn. White's plan consists of the construction of a wedge with a subsequent meeting of the counterattack ... f5 with g4. If Black refrains from ... f5, then he will not only turn out to be severely cramped by the wedge, but White will also have the possibility of developing a dangerous pawn attack on the king's flank by h4-h5. All these ""trumps" are exploited by White in the present game.
zh: 这是白方对抗老印度防御的一种长期存在的方式，并且最近在实践中变得越来越频繁。众所周知，在与斯梅斯洛夫的回归对局中，鲍特维尼克同样坚持了这样的开局处理。f-兵看似非常温和的举动具有重大的规划意义。它远远超出了简单地努力加强兵中心的主要链接之一——e4兵的限制。白方的计划包括构建楔子以及随后的反击……f5与g4。如果黑方不采取……f5，那么他不仅会被楔子严重挤压，而且白方也有可能通过h4-h5对兵发起危险的兵攻击。所有这些“王牌”都被白方在本局对局中利用了。

text: If Black does not take measures to determine the position in the centre, then, after Qd2 and O-O-O, White without difficulty develops a threatening attack on the king's flank (g4, h4-h5, Bh6) under the cover of the pawn centre. With this it becomes clear that Black submits to the construction of the opponent's wedge, intending, even after g4, to sharpen the game with the advance e ... f5.
zh: 如果黑方不采取措施确定中心位置，则在Qd2和O-O-O之后，白方在兵中心的掩护下，毫无困难地对王翼（g4、h4-h5、Bh6）发起威胁攻击。由此可见，黑方屈服于对手楔形的构建，即使在g4之后，仍打算通过先进的 e。。。 f5 来锐化棋局。

text: In his last match with Botvinnik, Smyslov tried to counter White's plan with energetic pawn play on the queen's flank (... a6, ...c6, and ... b5). This counterattacking idea has still not received sufficient practical trials; in any event it did not justify itself in the match.
zh: 在他与鲍特维尼克的最后一场对局中，斯梅斯洛夫试图在后翼（。。。a6、。。。c6和。。。b5）上用精力充沛的兵来反击怀特的计划。这种反击的想法还没有得到足够的实践检验；无论如何，它在对局中并没有证明自己的合理性。

text: Such a blockade of the c4 pawn is usually linked to an attack on the pawn wedge from the side of the queen's flank. Black strives in the future for ... a6 and ... b5. In the present game it does not come to this and the move ... c5 loses its clearness of purpose.
zh: 对c4兵的这种封锁通常与从后翼一侧对兵楔的攻击有关。布莱克在未来为。。。a6和。。。b5而奋斗。在目前的对局中，事情并没有发展到这一点，并且这一举动……c5失去了其明确的目的。

text: This position eloquently bears witness to how contemporary notions have changed concerning the opening struggle. According to classical principles, the principal opening task has still not been accomplished: the pieces are virtually undeveloped, it is mainly the pawns which have advanced (White's will make 7 moves out of the first 10!). And yet, despite the opinion of some opening theoreticians, the opening stage can be considered over. The plans of the opponents, particularly White, are determined, but the struggle of the plans - is already a process of the middlegame.
zh: 这一立场雄辩地证明了有关开场斗争的相反观念是如何发生变化的。根据经典原理，主要的开局任务还没有完成：棋子实际上还没有发展，主要是兵已经进步（白方将在前10步中走7步！）。然而，尽管一些开局理论家持不同意见，但开局阶段可以认为已经结束。对手的计划，特别是白方，已经确定，但计划的斗争 - 已经是中局的过程。

text: The diagrammed position was reached in two more encounters in the same tournament, i.e.: Tal- Boleslavsky (played earlier than the present game) and Kotov- Spassky (played later). text: Usually the phalanx breaks through the front and only then do the pieces rush into the attack. In this game it was the other way around. The attack began with the pieces, but then they had need of the pawn phalanx.

text: The attack of a pawn mass on the flanks is figuratively called a storm, but it does actually warrant this name since it develops impetuously, by force, and in the intense heat of the struggle. With castling on opposite sides, at times both opponents rush into the storm and success usually attends the one who first achieves pawn escort and begins to loosen the position of the enemy king. Not infrequently the pawn storm takes place also upon same-side castling or entirely without castling. In such cases the attacking side needs to watch closely for his own security, in voluntarily exposing his own king, and not allow the opponent to complicate the struggle by means of a counterattack.
zh: 兵侧翼的群众攻击被形象地称为风暴，但它实际上确实有这个名称，因为它是在激烈的斗争中以武力猛烈地发展的。由于易位在两侧，有时双方都会冲入风暴，成功通常属于第一个完成兵护送并开始放松敌人王阵势的人。兵潮也经常发生在同侧易位或完全没有易位。在这种情况下，攻击方需要密切关注自身安全，主动暴露自己的王，不要让对手通过反击使斗争复杂化。

text: The pawn storm column usually consists of three pawns, advancing side by side on the f, g, h or a, b, c files; ; there is also a two-pawn column. The pawn storm has more chances of success if the g or h pawns in the opponent's castled position have advanced. The contact of the storming column with such pawns takes place two tempi earlier than with pawns on their original squares, and as a consequence the general tempo of attack is apparently accelerated.
zh: 兵潮栏通常由三个兵组成，在f、g、h或a、b、c线上并列前进；；还有一个两兵列。如果对手城堡位置的g或h兵前进，兵潮成功的机会更大。冲锋纵队与这种兵的接触比与兵在其原始格上的接触要早两个时间，因此总体先手的攻击明显加速。

text: It is necessary to carefully calculate a pawn storm. However, this is a far from easy task. In the majority of cases a certain amount of risk is involved in the storm. Even when the pawn column achieves the aim and comes into contact with the opponent's pawns, one has to weigh up the character of the piece battle which must develop after the disappearance of pawns from the battle zone. It must not be forgotten that the advance of the pawn group creates s various positional weaknesses in the rear, and if the storm does not succeed then things might surprisingly ou, q o1 1no uin 1 better off than at the start'. Let us give some illustrations.
zh: 有必要仔细计算一个兵潮。然而，这绝非易事。在大多数情况下，风暴会带来一定的风险。即使兵纵队达到目的，与对方的兵接触，也必须权衡兵从战区消失后必然展开的棋子战斗的性质。不能忘记的是，兵小组的推进在后方造成了各种位置上的弱点，如果风暴没有成功，那么事情可能会出人意料地比开始时更好。让我们举一些例子。

text: In Vidmar-Tarrasch (Nurnberg 1906) White begins a pawn storm on the king's flank. The basis for this is the weakening of Black's castled position by the move ... h6 and the cramped position of his bishop on f6. He can do nothing in the centre and this makes the flank attack safe.
zh: 在 Vidmar-塔拉什 (纽伦堡 1906) 中，白方在王翼上开始兵潮。其基础是黑方的城堡位置被削弱了……h6，以及他的象在f6上的狭窄位置。他在中路无能为力，这使得侧翼进攻变得安全。

text: Let us look at a few games. To place the king under frontal attack from the infantry would, on his part, be foolhardy.

text: A colourful picture of a storm. Black is excellently mobilised, his knight is placed in the centre of the board on a weak square, both his rooks operate in the direction of the centre, one of them is located on the open c-file which leads straight to the haven of the enemy king. However, White is also attacking with his three-pawn storm-group, and this is his only, but very important, positional plus. With the next moves, his pawns enter into contact with the Black king's defensive cover, bring about necessary exchanges, and then White's piece army, in the first instance his queen and rook, begin to operate very powerfully against the breach which has been created on the file.
zh: 一幅暴风雨的彩色图画。黑方的动员能力非常出色，他的马被放置在棋盘中央的弱格上，他的两个车都朝着中心的方向运作，其中一个位于空旷的c线上，直接通向敌人的避难所王。然而，怀特也在用他的三兵潮组进攻，这是他唯一但非常重要的位置优势。接下来的动作中，他的兵与黑方王的防御掩护接触，进行必要的交锋，然后白方的棋子军队，首先是他的后和车，开始非常有力地对抗在线上造成的突破口。

text: The Struggle with Heavy Pieces

text: In the introduction we have already pointed out the presence of a highly significant difference e between the middlegame and endgame stages. The transition into the endgame to a considerable extent changes both the whole thematic struggle, which means also the planning of it, and methods of operation. It is very important to mention that in t the endgame the evaluation of weak and strong points is changed and also the significance of open lines, the role of theory and technique increases, and particular requirements for handling pawns arise.
zh: 在引言中我们已经指出了中局和残局阶段之间存在高度显着的差异。进入残局的过渡在很大程度上改变了整个主题斗争，这也意味着它的计划和操作方法。值得一提的是，在残局中，弱项和强项的评价发生了变化，开放线的重要性、理论和技术的作用也增加了，对运用兵的特殊要求也出现了。

text: In this connection the question inevitably arises: to what extent in the central stage of the game is it necessary to be guided by considerations coming out of the possibility of transferring the struggle to the endgame? You see the game of chess presents itself as a single whole and, despite the significant difference in the positional requirements of the middlegame and endgame, never should it be forgotten that in many cases even the most sharp and tense struggle in the middlegame receives its completion deep in the endgame.
zh: 与此相关，不可避免地会出现一个问题：在博弈的中央阶段，在多大程度上有必要以将斗争转移到残局的可能性为指导？你会看到国际象棋对局呈现为一个整体，尽管中局和残局的位置要求存在显着差异，但永远不应该忘记的是，在许多情况下，即使是中局中最激烈和最紧张的斗争也会在残局深处完成。

text: It is possible to reply to this question in a general way, that, taking into account the possibility of the future endgame, one should not exaggerate its role and so much the more attach decisive importance to the solving of the creative problems of the middlegame and even some openings.
zh: 可以笼统地回答这个问题，即考虑到未来残局的可能性，不应过分夸大其作用，而更应决定性地重视解决中局乃至某些开局的创造性问题。

text: Let us say there is no need to worsen one's pawn formation in vain, since this might have an unfavourable effect in the endgame. But if a concrete plan of action, intended in the middlegame, requires the creation of backward, doubled, isolated and even a formation of pawns, then it is necessary to go in for this by discarding abstract considerations, relevent only to the endgame.
zh: 可以说，没有必要徒劳地恶化兵阵型，因为这可能会对残局产生不利的影响。但是，如果中局的具体行动计划需要创建落后的、双重的、孤立的甚至是兵的阵型，那么就有必要通过放弃仅与残局相关的抽象考虑来实现这一点。

text: It is well-known, for example, that Lasker,by（ choosing the exchange variation of the Spanish Game as White (1 e4 e5 2 Nf3 Nc6 3 Bb5 a6 4 Bxc6), was planning, after 4 ... dxc6, to exploit the extra pawn on the king's flank in the endgame. He carried out this plan with success in match games against Janowski i and Tarrasch. This did not prevent Lasker, in the international tourmnament at Nirnberg 1896, finishing off Tarrasch in the same variation even before the transfer of the game into an ending. A still more striking example was the game Lasker-Capablanca (Petersburg 1914). Capablanca, familiar with Lasker's planned line to the endgame, in the exchange variation, blockaded the e-pawn and planned an attack on it with the rooks on the open e-file together with support from the bishop on b7. The struggle developed in the middlegame, in which Lasker did not stop at the advance f5, as a result of which the e4 pawn became backward and weak. At the decisive moment of the struggle he sacrificed this pawn, to invade with the knight on the sixth rank and the rooks on the seventh, and literally smashed his dangerous opponent. In conceiving the idea of attack, Lasker assessed his prospects finely and deeply and disregarded considerations about a possible endgame.
zh: 众所周知，例如拉斯克，通过（选择西班牙开局的兑换变例为白方（1 e4 e5 2 Nf3 Nc6 3 Bb5 a6 4Bxc6），计划在 4。。。 dxc6 之后，利用残局中王翼上的额外兵。他在与雅诺夫斯基 i和塔拉什的对局中成功地执行了这个计划。这并没有阻止拉斯克在1896年纽伦堡国际锦标赛中，甚至在对局转入结局之前以相同的变体完成塔拉什。一个更引人注目的例子是对局拉斯克-卡帕布兰卡 (彼得堡 1914)。卡帕布兰卡熟悉拉斯克到残局的计划路线，在兑换变例封锁了e-兵，并计划在e线上用车对其进行攻击，同时得到b7上象的支援。斗争发展到中局，拉斯克并没有止步于f5的前进，结果e4兵变得落后而无力。在战斗的决定性时刻，他弃子用这个兵，用马入侵第六个横线，车入侵第七个，并真正粉碎了他危险的对手。在构思进攻的想法时，拉斯克精细而深入地评估了他的前景，并忽略了对可能的结局的考虑。

text: In short, if it is possible to combine the positional requirements of the middlegame and endgame - so much the better. But if they clash, then preference must be given to the requirements of the middlegame.
zh: 简而言之，如果能够将中局和残局的位置要求结合起来，那就更好了。但如果它们发生冲突，则必须优先考虑中局的要求。

text: These questions arise in a particularly sharp fashion in positions where only queens and rooks on each side take part in the struggle (obviously, besides the pawns). The feature of this sort of middlegame position consists of the fact that the exchange of one of the pieces leads to an endgame - a queen or a rook. Here, calculation of the endgame situation becomes one of the most important factors for assessment.
zh: 当双方只有后和车参与斗争时（显然，除了兵），这些问题以特别尖锐的方式出现。这种中局局面的特点是，交换棋子之一会导致残局 - 后或车。这里，残局局势的计算成为最重要的评估因素之一。

text: In chess literature the opinion is expressed that it is necessary to treat positions with heavy piece material as an endgame. This is a profound error.
zh: 在国际象棋文献中，有人认为有必要将具有重子材料的局面视为残局。这是一个深刻的错误。

text: A characteristic feature of the concluding stage of the game is the full right of the king to take part in the struggle. The king in the endgame is an active piece, which frequently decides the outcome of the battle. Meanwhile, in the presence of the queen and rook, the king is obliged to seek shelter behind pawn cover, and forgetting this truth prompted by the mistaken notion that the struggle has proceeded to the endgame, might end and actually does end in a very sad way.
zh: 对局最后阶段的一个特点是王完全有权参与斗争。残局中的王是主动的棋子，常常决定战斗的结果。与此同时，在后和车在场的情况下，王不得不在兵的掩护下寻求庇护，并忘记了这一事实，因为错误的观念认为斗争已经进入了最后阶段，可能会结束并且实际上确实以一种非常悲伤的方式结束。

text: At the same time the king must be ready to rush immediately into battle the moment the queens are exchanged and a rook ending ensues. On the other hand, in positions where an exchange of one of the heavy pieces leads to the endgame phase, great attention has to be paid to the pawn formation, to see that it is as comfortable as possible for the end-stage. The presence of passed pawns is of particular significance. Often this advantage acquires a decisive character. You see it is necessary to bring to a halt the advance of a passed pawn, in the present case the role of a blockading piece is not appropriate for the king, while to waste the energy of a queen or rook on the blockade of a pawn means conceding an advantage in force to the opponent for the rest of the struggle.
zh: 同时，王必须做好准备，在交换后后立即投入战斗，并出现车结局。另一方面，在交换其中一个重子导致残局阶段的位置中，必须高度关注兵阵型，以确保其在最后阶段尽可能舒适。通兵的存在具有特别重要的意义。这种优势常常具有决定性的特征。你看，有必要阻止通兵的前进，在目前的情况下，封锁棋子的作用不适合王，而在后或车的封锁上浪费后或车的能量意味着在剩下的时间里让对手获得武力优势。奋斗。

text: The features of the struggle, inherent in this individual phase of the middlegame, also make up the contents of the present chapter.
zh: 中局这一单独阶段所固有的斗争特征也构成了本章的内容。

text: Here we have a position from the 5th match game Schlechter- Lasker (1910).
zh: 这里我们有第 5 场对局的位置施莱希特- 拉斯克 (1910)。

text: Can it be contended that either one of the sides has the advantage? Of course not. More than this, chessplayers would shake many hands s and go away peacefully.
zh: 可以说双方都占优势吗？当然不是。不仅如此，棋手还会与许多人握手，然后平静地离开。

text: On the board we are on the verge of an endgame, but this verge will last for many moves and will not be crossed.
zh: 在棋盘上，我们正处于残局的边缘，但这个边缘将持续很多步，并且不会被跨越。

text: In such positions, the loss of a pawn is tantamount to defeat; on the other hand the weakening of the b6 point plays no role at all.
zh: 在这种情况下，失去一个兵就等于失败；另一方面，b6点的减弱根本不起作用。

Black thereby begins to carry out a plan of enlivening the play on the queen's flank. At the same time a particular problem is also solved transfer of the function of defence of the d6 pawn to the king, which frees the queen from this role. The king is clearly more securely placed

text: White has ventured a sort of pawn storm, intending to create some threats to the Black king. Passive play is not to Lasker's taste and he boldly accepts the challenge.
zh: 白方尝试了某种兵潮，打算对黑方王造成一些威胁。被动的玩法不合拉斯克的口味，他大胆地接受了挑战。

text: Possibly a little risky, but a move which is full of initiative that poses White a serious problem. Black strives for a position in which an exchange of queens will be favourable for him. This allows him to achieve great freedom of activity in so far as White has to avoid the endgame. The negative side to the move is the rather weakened pawn cover of his king. Meanwhile it is still a long way to the endgame, indeed will he even succeed in achieving it.
zh: 可能有点冒险，但这一步充满了主动权，给白方带来了严重的问题。黑方努力争取一个交换后对他有利的位置。这使得他能够获得很大的活动自由度，而白方必须避免残局。此举的负面影响是他的王的兵掩护相当弱化。与此同时，距离最终的目标还有很长的路要走，他是否真的能成功呢？

text: With the aim of avoiding variations, analogous to that cited in the previous note, and likewise guaranteeing a post nearer to the centre for the king. Now, however, the h3 3 pawn is weakened. It is interesting that Schlechter, a brilliant representative of the Vienna school, in the creative work of which the exploitation of positional weaknesses was achieved with filigree technique, nevertheless decides on this.

text: Now the rook can be transferred in the shortest time for play on both flanks. It also prepares a demonstration against the h3 pawn. The position is appreciably sharpened.
zh: 现在，车可以在最短的时间内转移到两侧。它还准备举行反对h3兵的示威活动。位置明显锐化。

zh: Kb6。现在拉斯克的举动很明确：f-兵不再受到攻击。43 后 Rxg7 Re4 黑方必须赢得残局。

Ra8, in order to radically do away with White's main and perhaps only chance, consisting C of the advance of the a-pawn. It is possible that Lasker, not seeing a clear way to further strengthen his position, in his turn decides to provoke Schlechter into the following bayonet attack, placing his hopes on the fact that this is associated with material sacrifices.

text: White might not get another opportunity. Soon Black will be convinced that it is not so easy to defend his king even against the comparatively small 1 numbers of attacking forces.
zh: 白方可能不会再有机会了。很快黑方就会相信，即使是相对较小的 1 个数字攻击力量，防守他的王也不是那么容易。

zh: 44 Kg3 Qg1+ 并获胜。然而，拉斯克急于制造子力收益，更使得王没有明显的直接危险。

zh: 因此黑方赢得了兵。但总体而言，白方有什么回报吗？毫无疑问是的。敌人王的兵掩体进一步松开，线被打开，直接瞄准其位置。白方威胁要吃主动权。

zh: 拉斯克对此当然没有信心，而且，由于他通常低估了对手的机会，因此他认为自己有权取得更多成就。

text: The failure of the general offensive in the centre, fatigue from the opponent's never-ending threats all this, apparently, served as a reason for Lasker's making a mistake. However, the Black king has fallen into such a dangerous position that a draw was already the best way out of the position for him. For this he should play 54 ...

text: The whole ending serves as an instructive example of the underestimation of middlegame ideas in the struggle e with heavy pieces. Strictly speaking, Lasker made only one, but nevertheless a principal mistake. He yielded too much to the mercy of endgame ideas.
zh: 整个结局是在与重子斗争中低估中局思想的一个有启发性的例子。严格来说，拉斯克只犯了一个错误，但仍然是一个主要错误。他太多地屈服于残局想法的摆布。

text: This example reveals sufficiently clearly the peculiarities and difficulties associated with defence and attack in the struggle of heavy pieces. The following ending perhaps even more distinctly illustrates these features and difficulties, and likewise the character of mistakes made in such positions even by 1 masters of the highest class.
zh: 这个例子足够清楚地揭示了重子斗争中与防御和攻击相关的特殊性和困难。下面的结局也许更清楚地说明了这些特征和困难，以及即使是最高级别的大师在这种情况下所犯错误的特征。

text: The game Lasker-Pillsbury, played in the international tournament at Hastings 1895, reached the diagrammed position
zh: 1895 年哈斯廷斯国际锦标赛中进行的对局拉斯克-皮尔斯伯里到达了图中所示的位置

text: White's central pawns are isolated and weak, his king is in need of defence. Black already has an extra pawn, the exchange of any of the pieces makes it easier for him to realise his material advantage in the endgame: in short, he has every chance of victory. This is how both partners assessed the state of affairs during the game.
zh: 白方的中路兵孤立且薄弱，他的王需要防守。黑方已经多了一个兵，交换任何一个棋子都可以让他在残局中更容易实现自己的子力优势：总之，他有获胜的机会。这是双方在对局期间评估事态的方式。

text: Admittedly 1 a dynamic assessment of the position points to a certain weakness of the Black a7 and c7 pawns, but the need for White to defend his king and e4 pawn makes it difficult to exploit the minuses in the opponent's pawn skeleton.
zh: 诚然，1 对局面的动态评估指出了黑方 a7 和 c7 兵的某些弱点，但是白方需要防守他的王和 e4 兵，这使得很难利用对手兵骨架中的缺点。

text: Let us look at how further events developed in this difficult position.
zh: 让我们看看在这种困难的情况下事件的进一步发展如何。

text: The leap of a wounded tiger! It is reminiscent of the "desperate' play of Schlechter in the previous game. White has nothing to lose and he bravely I goes in for an exchange of his central pawn for the flank one of his opponent. On 23 Qf3, which, possibly, would be preferred by other chessplayers, could follow 23 ... Qd4+ 24 Kh1 Qg7 with the threat of exchanges on the f-file.
zh: 受伤的老虎的跳跃！这让人想起上一场对局中施莱希特的“绝望”玩法。怀特没有什么可失去的，他勇敢地用他的中央兵交换对手的侧翼。在23 Qf3上，这可能是其他棋手更喜欢的，可以遵循23。。。 Qd4+ 24Kh1 Qg7 并威胁在 f线上进行交流。

Thus, for example, the queen ending will be acceptable for White, while in some cases, if Black does not manage to blockade the passed pawn in time with the king, even the rook ending. Therefore Pillsbury should prefer 24 ... c4 after which both 25

text: The significance of the extra pawn has been appreciably neutralised.
zh: 额外的兵的重要性已被明显抵消。

text: This move bears witness to the fact that Pillsbury did not try to understand sufficiently deeply the situation which has arisen.I By removing g the rook from the back rank, he dooms the queen to the role of watchman for the passed pawn.N Meanwhile, in the forthcoming struggle, the energy of the queen is needed for the fulfilment of another task. It is therefore no surprise that soon Black not only proves to be powerless to realise his advantage but also a real threat of defeat hangs over him. The rook move also has another shady side it worsens the position of the Black king, with which the rook now loses contact. In making his aggressive t thrust, Pillsbury obviously counted on enlivening the passed e-pawn and, by threatening to advance it, to avert or to some extent weaken the offensive power of the enemypassed pawn. However, very soon it becomes clear that this plan is mistaken and that the passed a-pawn in the present situation is more advanced and dangerous than the e-pawn. Pillsbury's idea proves to be insufficiently concrete, he cannot foresee, with necessary distinctness, a way of leading to the achievement of the planned objective.
zh: 这一举动证明了皮尔斯伯里没有试图足够深入地了解所出现的情况。I通过将车从横线后面移除，他注定了后成为通兵守望者的角色。N同时，在即将到来的斗争中，后的能量需要为后提供能量。完成另一项任务。因此，毫不奇怪，很快黑方不仅无力实现自己的优势，而且真正的失败威胁笼罩着他。车举动还有另一个阴暗面，它使黑方王的位置恶化，车现在与黑方王失去联系。皮尔斯伯里在做出侵略性的t冲刺时，显然是指望激活已通过的e-兵，并通过威胁推进来避免或在一定程度上削弱敌人的攻击力通兵。然而，很快就发现这个计划是错误的，目前情况下通过的a-兵比e-兵更先进、更危险。皮尔斯伯里的想法被证明不够具体，他无法以必要的清晰度预见到实现计划目标的方法。

text: Up to this fatal last move, Pillsbury could still nourish some hopes of realising his material advantage. It was necessary to reinforce the e-pawn from behind, by playing 29 Re8. After the possible 30 a5 d5 31 Qe2 e4 32 Ra1

zh: Ra8机会仍然在黑方。即使犯了错误，皮尔斯伯里也应该立即通过返回车到 b8 来纠正它。欲始终如一，从此走下坡路；从心理学的角度来看，一个有趣的国际象棋情节。

zh: 白方威胁 33 Qf2，如果 33。。。 Qe7，则 34 a7；简而言之，乌云笼罩着黑方的局面。因此 32。。。 Rb8 是必须的，之后他仍然可以继续战斗，但已经只能打平了。这是通过 33 Qg3 实现的

text: The winning move. White has deprived the Black rook of the possibility of returning tot the eighth rank, and the a-pawn in the end completes its victorious march.
zh: 制胜之举。白方剥夺了黑方车重返第八横线的可能性，a-兵最终完成了胜利的进军。

text: The White passed pawn achieves its objective first: 34 ... e2 35 a7. The ill-fated rook on b4 is out of play. On 34 ... ( Qa7 White simply captures the e3 pawn.
zh: 白方通兵首先实现其目标：34。。。 e2 35 a7。b4 上命运多舛的车已出局。在 34。。。 ( Qa7 白方简单地吃掉了 e3 兵。

text: The struggle proved to be very instructive in the ending of the 15th game of the return match Euwe-Alekhine (1937).
zh: 事实证明，这场斗争在回归赛尤伟-阿廖欣（1937年）第15局对局的结尾中非常有启发性。

text: White has a passed pawn, indeed one which is furthermore defended from behind. In the rook and queen endings this guarantees him an indisputable positional advantage. However, with queen and rook on the board, a number of other factors influence the assessment of the position. In the present case, for example, it is necessary to pay attention to the strong position of the Black rook on the second rank, where it is far actively placed than the more White rook. A comparison of the positions of the kings likewise proves to be in Black's favour in view of the presence of the "vent" h6. He has a strong mobile pawn in the centre. White has a weak point on f2. In such a situation White's passed pawn on a4 might be converted from a strength into a weakness, and this is confirmed by the immediate course of events.
zh: 白方有一张通兵，实际上也是从后面防守的。在车和后结局中，这保证了他无可争议的位置优势。然而，由于后和车在董事会，许多其他因素会影响职位的评估。例如，在当前情况下，需要注意第二个横线上黑方车的强势位置，它比白方车处于更活跃的位置。鉴于“通风口”h6 的存在，王位置的比较同样证明对黑方有利。他在中心有一个强大的移动兵。白方在f2上有弱点。在这种情况下，白方 a4 上的通兵可能会从优势转变为劣势，这一点已被立即发生的事件所证实。

text: An "obvious" move, apparently made in the firm conviction of the superiority of his position. But the fact of the matter is that with each step forward the passed pawn is only weakened, and it soon becomes very difficult to defend it. He should play 27 h3, creating a "vent" for the White king.
zh: 这是一个“明显”的举动，显然是出于对自己地位优越性的坚定信念而做出的。但事实是，每前进一步，通兵只会被削弱，并且很快就会变得非常难以防御。他应该下27 h3，为白方王创造一个“通风口”。

text: Ra2, and the a-pawn is already doomed to destruction; also no

zh: 斗争的进一步进程偏离了我们的主题，对局最终以平局告终。

text: The conclusion is clear: upon a struggle of heavy pieces there is possible such a combination of factors, particularly in association with the position of the king, which is capable of depreciating the role of even an extremely well-defended and far-advanced passed pawn. Those who are inclined to look at such a struggle as a process of the endgame are deeply and hopelessly mistaken.
zh: 结论很明确：在重子的斗争中，可能存在这样的因素组合，特别是与王的地位相关，它甚至能够贬低防御极其严密和先进的通兵的作用。那些倾向于将这种斗争视为终局过程的人是深深且无可救药的错误。

text: In the diagram is shown a position reached in Romanovsky- Stahlberg, (Moscow 1935):
zh: 图中显示了罗曼诺夫斯基-斯塔尔贝里中到达的位置（莫斯科 1935）：

text: Despite the equality of forces and relative simplicity of the position, White has a basis for considering his position preferable. His pawns are more compactly placed, the Black c5 pawn is isolated and is an object for pressure. Nevertheless, White's chances of victory must be regarded as being minimal. There is no way for White to increase t the a attack on the c5 pawn, t the number of operating forces on the board is very limited, the d3 pawn cannot go to the help of its pieces since the d4 square, where it might come into contact with the c5 pawn, is firmly blockaded. It is to White's advantage to force a rook ending in order to activate his king, but it is quite difficult to achieve this. However, generally speaking, his king is worse placed than the enemy king, which is reliably covered with pawns. And yet the initiative is undoubtedly White's hands. Black is chained to passive defence and must watch closely in case the enemy attempts to display activity somewhere.
zh: 尽管力量平等且立场相对简单，怀特有理由认为他的立场更可取。他的兵放置得更紧凑，黑c5兵是孤立的，是一个压力对象。尽管如此，白方获胜的机会必须被认为是微乎其微的。白方没有办法增加对c5兵的攻击，棋盘上的操作力量非常有限，d3兵无法从d4格开始帮助其棋子，在那里它可能会与d4格接触。c5兵，被牢牢封锁。为了激活他的王而强制采用车结局对白方有利，但实现这一点相当困难。然而，一般来说，他的王的位置比敌人王差，而敌人王确实被兵覆盖。然而主动权无疑是白方的手。黑方处于被动防御状态，必须密切关注，以防敌人试图在某处表现出活动。

text: What should White's plan consist of? At the first stage his main task must be to drive away the enemy queen from the central d5 position and occupy the c4 square with his queen, where it will be far more actively placed. Upon this, White must be ready to exchange queens and thus to transfer the struggle into a rook endgame. In this connection he must create as favourable conditions as possible for such an endgame.
zh: 白方的计划应该包括哪些内容？在第一阶段，他的主要任务必须是将敌人后从中央d5位置赶走，并用他的后占领c4格，在那里它将更加积极地放置。在此基础上，白方必须准备好交换后，从而将斗争转移到车残局。在这方面，他必须为这样的结局创造尽可能有利的条件。

text: We look at White's future operations in more detail. Above all he must move his king up as close as possible to the centre, let us say to the f2 square, while in the rook endgame he will prepare the advance e3 followed by d4 with the rooks s placed on the c-file. This leads to the win of the c5 pawn, providing of course, that the opponent himself does not succeed in bringing his king to the centre.
zh: 我们更详细地了解怀特未来的运营。最重要的是，他必须将他的王尽可能靠近中心移动，比如说 f2 格，而在车残局中，他将准备前进 e3，然后是 d4，并将车放在 c线上。这将导致 c5 兵获胜，当然前提是对手本人没有成功地将他的王带到中心。

text: From this it is clear that White's task is far from easy, while, upon good defence by Black, possibly unrealisable. In any case, there is a sharp, tense struggle in prospect, sated with various interesting ideas.
zh: 由此可见，白方的任务绝非易事，而如果黑方防守良好，则可能无法完成。无论如何，前景中存在着一场尖锐、紧张的斗争，充满了各种有趣的想法。

text: 36. Qc3 Rc6 37. Qc2 Kh8 38. Kf2
zh: 36. Qc3 Rc6 37. Qc2 Kh8 38. Kf2

text: The advance of the king to the centre points to the fact that White is striving to transfer to the endgame. If, at this moment, the Black king cannot in good time support the engagement in the centre, then after the exchange of queens White would l create an attack on the c5 pawn by one of two means: f4 and d4, or e3 and likewise d4.
zh: 王向中心的推进表明白方正在努力转移到残局。如果此时黑方王无法及时支持中心交战，那么在交换后后，白方将通过f4和d4或e3和d4两种方式之一对c5兵发起攻击。

text: To a certain extent, these threats are also hanging with queens present, but the carrying out of them in the middlegame involves danger (as we have already had the opportunity of convincing ourselves in the model game Schlechter-Lasker) in view of the exposed position of his own king.
zh: 在某种程度上，这些威胁也伴随着后的存在，但在中局中实施这些威胁是有危险的（因为我们已经有机会在模型对局施莱希特-拉斯克中说服自己），因为他自己的王暴露了位置。

text: Consequently, Black must place his king in such a way that, in the event of an endgame, it is able to quickly go over to the defence of the c5 pawn, while if it is attacked by the heavy pieces it can easily find shelter on the flank. From this point of view, the most convenient square was f7 and it was in fact necessary to direct the king here by playing now 38 Kg8. Black thought otherwise and, judging by the future development of events, less well.
zh: 因此，黑方必须将其王放置在这样的位置，即在残局的情况下，它能够快速转入c5兵的防守，而如果它受到重子的攻击，它可以轻松地在侧翼找到庇护。从这个角度来看，最方便的格是f7，实际上需要通过现在播放38Kg8来将王引导到这里。布莱克的想法并非如此，而且从事态的未来发展来看，情况不太好。

text: This storming thrust gains in strength with the position of the king on g6. In making this, White pursues three aims: to create another weakness for the opponent in the centre - an isolated pawn on e5; to create a handy piece base on the e4 square, which the king can also exploit in the event of an endgame ensuing; finally to generally open the position in the centre and bare the cover of the enemy king. Nevertheless the energetic advance of the White e-pawn sharpens the struggle for both sides - you see the position of his own king is exposed, the d3 pawn, located on an open file, becomes backward.
zh: 随着王在g6上的位置，这种猛烈的推力会增强。在这样做时，怀特追求三个目标：为中间的对手创造另一个弱点 - 孤兵上的 e5；在 e4 格的基础上创建一个方便的棋子，王也可以在随后的残局中利用它；最后大致打开中心阵地，暴露敌人的掩护王。然而，白e-兵的积极推进加剧了双方的斗争——你会看到他自己的王的位置暴露了，位于开放线上的d3兵变得落后。

text: Little by little, White prepares for the endgame. This move is made so that the h-pawn will not find itself under attack in the event of the exchange of queens and a check of the Black rook on the second rank. On the other hand, White wants to ascertain the position of the Black king: the move to f6 is unfavourable because of the reply f4, while the retreat to f8 means taking it away from the important central squares. In this way the advance of the h-pawn is, as it were, a useful waiting move.
zh: 白方逐渐为残局做准备。进行此移动是为了在交换后并检查第二个横线上的黑方车时，h-兵不会发现自己受到攻击。另一方面，白方想要确定黑方王的位置：由于答复f4，下棋到f6是不利的，而退到f8则意味着远离重要的中心格。这样，冲兵就可以说是一个有用的等待着棋。

text: In this way, Stahlberg could force a draw. Stahlberg distrustfully draws the White king to an open position, and too trustily - to an endgame with equal material. text: Before drawing conclusions let us look at one more game - this time fully, because in itself it seems to sum up our observations. In it nearly all the specific characteristics of interest to our theme are expressed, and the attack on an insufficiently secure king's position is particularly highlighted.
zh: 在得出结论之前，让我们再看一场对局——这一次是全面的，因为它本身似乎总结了我们的观察结果。其中几乎表达了我们主题感兴趣的所有具体特征，并且特别强调了对不够安全的王立场的攻击。

text: It remains for us to sum up a little. This amounts to the following: the struggle of heavy pieces of the type we have looked at is a process of the middlegame, and an attempt to include the king as an active piece in this struggle is just as risky as when it occurs in any middlegame; in addition to this, in the struggle of heavy pieces, several endgame factors (the role of the passed pawn etc.) increase in significance, while such operations as a pawn storm, various pawn formations in the centre and so on, on the other hand lose their effectiveness to a large extent; the struggle of heavy pieces is usually distinguished by great sharpness, in so far as it contains as much range of activity as is possible, and can quickly shift to any part of the board.
zh: 我们还有待一点总结。这相当于：我们所看到的类型的重子的斗争是一个中间对局的过程，并且尝试将王作为主动的棋子包含在这场斗争中与在任何中间对局中发生时一样危险；除此之外，在重子的斗争中，一些残局因素（通兵的作用等）的重要性增加，而诸如兵潮、各种兵中间阵型等操作则在很大程度上失去了效力；重子的斗争通常以极大的尖锐性为特征，因为它包含尽可能多的活动范围，并且可以快速转移到棋盘的任何部分。

text: Manoeuvring. About the Initiative
zh: 调动与主动权

text: In chess works and commentaries we quite often come across the term 'manoeuvering". Following the example of the late grandmaster Tartakover, it is sometimes substituted for the concept of "tacking", though in the semantic sense both terms are not the same.
zh: 在国际象棋著作和评论中，我们经常遇到“调动”这个术语。以已故大师塔塔科维为例，它有时会代替“tacking”的概念，尽管在语义上这两个术语并不相同。

text: Manoeuvering is a term coming from the German word manover, which manoeuvre.
zh: 调动是一个来自德语单词 manover 的术语，即运子。

text: means However, one should not mix up the concepts of "manoeuvre" and "manoeuvering". Manoeuvre - this is several moves of one piece, usually made with some sort of concrete aim. Manoeuvering - is a series of manoeuvres with different pieces, bearing a more or less prolonged c character and rarely having a clearly outlined aim.
zh: 表示但是，不应混淆“运子”和“调动”的概念。运子 - 这是一个棋子的几个动作，通常是为了某种具体的目标而进行的。调动 - 是一系列具有不同棋子的运子，具有或多或少较长的c字符，并且很少有明确概述的目标。

text: Manoeuvering is a concept that arose in connection with a definite phenomenon on the horizons of chess art which appeared at the end of the last century and was provoked mainly by the advocating of dogmatism by a number of representatives of the English and German chess schools.
zh: 调动是一个与上世纪末出现在国际象棋艺术视野中的特定现象有关的概念，主要是由英国和德国国际象棋流派的一些代表提倡教条主义引起的。

text: In a number of events, with these masters came to be recommended a form of waiting tactics. One of the partners, following this recommendation, waited until his opponent finally created a real weakness in his camp or made some other sort of mistake. It would also happen that both partners, having learned to be patient, began to manoeuvre by themselves in the rear of communications, following a policy of extreme caution and trying not to give each other even if only the slightest chance of attack.
zh: 在许多事件中，这些大师开始推荐一种等待策略。其中一位合伙人按照这一建议，等到他的对手最终在他的阵营中制造了一个真正的弱点或犯了一些其他类型的错误。也有可能，双方都学会了耐心，开始运子独自站在通讯后方，遵循极其谨慎的政策，尽量不给对方哪怕是最轻微的攻击机会。

text: This, of course, did not mean that all manoeuvering merited censure.
zh: 当然，这并不意味着所有调动都应该受到谴责。

text: In manoeuvering one can perceive several gradations. Besides waiting, aimless manoeuvring, there is also forcing, planning manoeuvring. This takes place in those cases where the achievement of the intended aim requires prolonged piece and pawn manoeuvres. This aspect of manoeuvering is seen particularly often in positions of a closed t type, that is with mutually locked pawn chains.
zh: 在调动中，人们可以感知到几个层次。除了等待、漫无目的调动，还有强迫、计划调动。当实现预期目标需要延长棋子和兵运子时，就会发生这种情况。调动的这个方面特别常见于闭合 t 类型的位置，即具有相互锁定的兵链。

text: We also begin our review with positions of this sort - and playing them is difficult and requires a profound and penetrating assessment of positions from the chessplayer.
zh: 我们也从这类棋局开始我们的审查——下棋很困难，需要棋手对棋局进行深刻而深入的评估。

zh: 白方：Em.拉斯克

text: Black: M.Chigorin
zh: 黑方：M.齐果林

text: (Hastings 1895)
zh: （哈斯廷斯1895）

text: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Bg4 3. c4 Bxf3 4 gxf3. Nc6 5. Nc3 e6 6. e3 Bb4 7 cxd5. Qxd5
zh: 1. d4 d5 2. Nf3 Bg4 3. c4 Bxf3 4 gxf3. Nc6 5. Nc3 e6 6. e3 Bb4 7 cxd5. Qxd5

text: The game has developed in a rather sharp and tense way and it is difficult to imagine that five moves later it already enters the area of protracted manoeuvering.
zh: 对局的发展相当尖锐和紧张，很难想象五步之后就已经进入了持久战调动的区域。

text: 8. Bd2 Bxc3 9. bxc3 Nge7 10 Rg1. Qh5 11. Qb3 Nd8 12. Qb5+
zh: 8. Bd2 Bxc3 9. bxc3 Nge7 10 Rg1. Qh5 11. Qb3 Nd8 12. Qb5+

text: White forces the exchange of queens, so as to make it easier for himself to exploit the "power of the two bishops".
zh: 白方强制交换后，以便让自己更容易利用“双象的力量”。

text: There are chessplayers (and at the time when the present game was played there were many of them amongst t the strongest masters of the world) who see the possession of the two bishops as a particular aspect of a positional advantage. We set out our point of view on this question in the following chapter.
zh: 有些棋手（在玩本对局时，他们中的许多人都是世界上最强大的大师）将拥有双象视为位置优势的一个特定方面。我们将在下一章阐述我们对这个问题的看法。

text: Bd3 From this moment, the struggle prolonged period of enters a manoeuvering, which will be continued almost to the very end of the encounter. The next pawn exchange follows only after 20 moves, while the next piece - after a full 40 moves, being at the same time a manoeuvre which wins the game.
zh: Bd3从这一刻起，战斗漫长的时期进入了调动，几乎会持续到战斗的最后。下一个兵交换仅在 20 步之后进行，而下一个棋子 - 在整整 40 步之后，同时成为赢得对局的运子。

text: White plans to double rooks on the g-file and then attack with h4. This looks quite threatening but is parried by comparatively simple means.
zh: 白方计划在 g线上加倍车，然后用 h4 进攻。这看起来很有威胁，但可以通过相对简单的手段来防御。

text: Regarding the manoeuvering of the partners in the present game, it bears a far more purposeful, planning character than in the previous examples.
zh: 关于本对局中伙伴的调动，它比前面的例子具有更有目的性、更有计划性的特征。

text: Consistent (White now threatens to decide the game after 19 h4 or even stronger 19 f5 exf5 20 Bxf5 Rc7 21 h4) but ... ignoring the opponent's idea.
zh: 一致（白方现在威胁要在 19 h4 甚至更强的 19 f5 exf5 20 Bxf5 Rc7 21 h4 后决定对局）但是。。。。。。忽略对手的想法。

text: Better is at once 18 f5 exf5 19
zh: 更好的是立即 18 f5 exf5 19

text: Bxf5. Rc7 20 Ragl cxd4 21. cxd4
zh: Bxf5。Rc7 20 拉格尔 cxd4 21. cxd4

text: Kh8. Though the threat of h4 is parried, the White pieces will be quite active in the roomy, opened position.
zh: Kh8。虽然 h4 的威胁被招架，但白方棋子在宽敞、开放的位置上将非常活跃。

text: 18 ... c4 19. Bc2 f5 20. Bc1 Rf7 21. Ba3 Rc6 22. Bc5 Ra6 23. a4 Nc6 24. Rb1 Rd7 25. Rgg1 Nge7 26. Rb2 Nd5 27. Kd2 Ra5 28 Rgb1. b6 29. Ba3 g6 30. Rb5 Ra6 31. Bc1 Nd8
zh: 18 ... c4 19. Bc2 f5 20. Bc1 Rf7 21. Ba3 Rc6 22. Bc5 Ra6 23. a4 Nc6 24. Rb1 Rd7 25. Rgg1 Nge7 26. Rb2 Nd5 27. Kd2 Ra5 28 Rgb1. b6 29. Ba3 g6 30. Rb5 Ra6 31. Bc1 Nd8

text: Though Black is forced into manoeuvering, this is far from being wait-and-see. He wants to provoke the move f3 through the threat of penetration with the knight on e4, and then to organise an attack on the enemy pawns in the centre.
zh: 尽管黑方被迫进入调动，但这远非观望。他想通过e4上的马进行渗透威胁来引发f3行动，然后组织对中心敌人兵的攻击。

text: 32. Ra1 Nf7 33. Rbb1 Nd6
zh: 32. Ra1 Nf7 33. Rbb1 Nd6

text: In his manoeuvering plan, Black undoubtedly yis thinking about opening the g-file, for which he has at his disposal the move ... g5. He reserves this option until later, taking into account the isolated position of his rook on a6, which, after the opening of the position, will not easily find harmonious co-operation with the other pieces.
zh: 在他的调动计划中，黑方毫无疑问正在考虑开g线，为此他可以采取走棋。。。g5。考虑到他的车在a6上的孤立位置，他将这个选项保留到以后，在开仓后，将不容易与其他棋子找到和谐的合作。

text: Nevertheless, Steinitz considered that the immediate 33 ... g5
zh: 尽管如此，斯坦尼茨认为立即 33。。。 g5

text: 34. fxg5 Nxg5 35. Ra3 Ne4+ 36
zh: 34. fxg5 Nxg5 35. Ra3 Ne4+ 36

text: Bxe4 fxe4 followed by 37 ... Rg7 should lead to a winning attack. Later Levenfish was to point out that, instead of 35 Ra3, 35 Bb2 is bolder for White, but also in this case, after 35 ... Ne4+ 36 Bxe4 fxe4, Black's dominating knight obliges one to evaluate the position in his favour. Admittedly, his advantage would hardly be sufficient for victory. White could continue 37 Rg1+ Rg7 38 Rxg7+ Kxg7 39 Ke2, preparing f3. He will find quite good resources to stubbornly fight for a draw.
zh: Bxe4 fxe4 后面跟着 37。。。 Rg7 应该会导致获胜的攻击。后来列文菲什指出，对于白方来说，35Bb2不是35Ra3，而是更大胆，但在这种情况下，在35。。。Ne4+36Bxe4fxe4之后，黑方的统治马迫使人们评估他的位置赞成。诚然，他的优势不足以取得胜利。白方可以继续 37 Rg1+ Rg7 38 Rxg7+ Kxg7 39 Ke2，准备 f3。他会找到相当好的资源来顽强地争取平局。

text: Preparing against the move ... g5, White frees his king from defence of the c3 pawn.
zh: 准备对抗这一步。。。g5，白方将他的王从c3兵的防御中释放出来。

text: It is interesting that even after this move, which opens the position, manoeuvering prevails over the game for more than 20 moves.
zh: 有趣的是，即使在这步打开局面的棋之后，调动仍然在 20 多步棋中占据主导地位。

text: Some commentators of this wonderfully creative game have expressed the opinion that Black should have preferred a waiting prophylactic line, striving to prevent the advance e4 and thereby limiting his immediate problems. Not to mention the fact that Chigorin was sickened by passive tactics, it is very doubtful whether Black could prevent the advance of the e-pawn. For example, 35
zh: 这场创意十足的棋局的一些评论员表示，黑方应该选择等待预防线，努力阻止前进e4，从而限制他眼前的问题。且不说齐果林已经被被动战术所困扰，黑方能否阻止冲兵也很值得怀疑。例如，35

text: Nd6 36. Ke2 Rf7 37. Bd2 Kf8 38. Kf2 Ke7 39. Kg3 Nf6 40. Raa1, upon
zh: Nd6 36. Ke2 Rf7 37. Bd2 Kf8 38. Kf2 Ke7 39. Kg3 Nf6 40. Raa1，

text: which White transfers one rook to f1, the other - to el and for all that carries out the break e4, but by now with three times the power.
zh: 白方将一个车转移到 f1，另一个 - 到 el 以及所有执行中断的 e4，但现在力量是三倍。

text: 36. Ke2 gxf4 37. e4 Nf6 38. Bxf4 Nh5 39. Be3 f4 40. Bf2 Ra5 41 Rg1+ Kf8 42. Raa1 e5 43. Rab1 Ng7 44. Rb4 Rc7 45. Bb1 Ne6 46 Rd1. Ned8!
zh: 36. Ke2 gxf4 37. e4 Nf6 38. Bxf4 Nh5 39. Be3 f4 40. Bf2 Ra5 41 Rg1+ Kf8 42. Raa1 e5 43. Rab1 Ng7 44. Rb4 Rc7 45. Bb1 Ne6 46 Rd1. Ned8!

text: Black threatens to win a pawn
zh: 黑方威胁要赢得兵

text: by ... Nc6. 47 ... Ba2 does not
help, in view of 47 ... Nc6, and, if
zh: 帮助，鉴于 47。。。 Nc6，并且，如果

text: 48. Rxc4, then 48 ... Nd6. 47. Rd2

White decides to give up a pawn, counting on opening the position and gaining space for his bishops to operate. Incidentally, in the first period of his creative work, Lasker was a great admirer of "the two bishops".
zh: 白方决定放弃兵，指望打开局面并为他的象赢得操作空间。顺便说一下，在创作的第一阶段，拉斯克是“双象”的崇拜者。

text: 47 ... Nc6 48. Rb5 Rxa4 49. dxe5 Nfxe5 50. Bh4 Rg7 51. Kf2 Rg6 52. Rdd5 Ra1 53. Bd8 Nd3+ 54 Bxd3. cxd3 55. Rxd3 Rag1 56 Rf5+ Kg8
zh: 47 ... Nc6 48. Rb5 Rxa4 49. dxe5 Nfxe5 50. Bh4 Rg7 51. Kf2 Rg6 52. Rdd5 Ra1 53. Bd8 Nd3+ 54 Bxd3. cxd3 55. Rxd3 Rag1 56 Rf5+ Kg8

text: The planned manoeuvering has been completed with an economical mating position. On 57 Rxf4 follows 57 ... R6g2+ 58 Ke3 Rel mate. Therefore he has to part with the bishop and after 57 Bg5 R6xg5 Lasker resigned.
zh: 计划的调动已完成，并具有经济的配合位置。在 57 Rxf4 上，接着是 57。。。 R6g2+ 58 Ke3 相关伙伴。因此他必须与象分手，并在57 Bg5 R6xg5 拉斯克之后辞职。

text: The following game is also a brilliant illustration of 40 moves of purposeful planning.
zh: 下面的对局也是 40 步有目的的计划的精彩例证。

text: English Opening
zh: 英国式开局

text: White: A.Alekhine
zh: 白方：A.阿廖欣

text: Black:F.Yates
zh: 黑方：F.耶茨

text: (Semmering 1926)
1. c4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4 d4. exd4 5. Nxd4 Bb4 6. Bg5 O-O.
zh: 1. c4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. Nf3 Nf6 4 d4. exd4 5. Nxd4 Bb4 6. Bg5 O-O.

text: Black chooses an unfortunate moment to castle, as a result of which the pinned knight becomes the "Achilles Heel" of his position. Alekhine called castling a colourless continuation. He should play 6
zh: 黑方选择了一个不幸的时刻来城堡，结果被钉住的马成为他的位置的“阿喀琉斯之踵”。阿廖欣称为易位无色后续手段。他应该打6

text: h6 7. Bh4 Bxc3+8. bxc3 7. Rc1 Re8 8. e3 d6 9. Be2 Ne5
zh: h6 7. Bh4 Bxc3+8. bxc3 7. Rc1 Re8 8. e3 d6 9. Be2 Ne5

text: Also here 9 ... h6 might still be useful.
zh: 同样在这里 9。。。 h6 可能仍然有用。

text: 10. O-O Bxc3 11. Rxc3 Ng6?
zh: 10. O-O Bxc3 11. Rxc3 Ng6?

text: A slight mistake, which for Alekhine, however, proves to be sufficient to win the game.
zh: 然而，对于阿廖欣来说，一个小小的错误足以赢得对局。

text: 11 ... h6 was also necessary now.
zh: 11。。。 h6 现在也是必要的。

text: 12. Nb5! Bd7
zh: 12. Nb5! Bd7

text: He cannot avoid doubled pawns on the f-file.
zh: 他无法在f线上避开叠兵。

text: 13. Bxf6 gxf6 14. Bd3 Kh8 15 Nd4. Rg8 16. Qh5 Qf8 17. f4 Re8 18. Rf3 Rg7 19. Nf5 Bxf5 20 Bxf5. Qe7
zh: 13. Bxf6 gxf6 14. Bd3 Kh8 15 Nd4. Rg8 16. Qh5 Qf8 17. f4 Re8 18. Rf3 Rg7 19. Nf5 Bxf5 20 Bxf5. Qe7

text: The Black king's position is seriously weakened, the f6, f7 and h7 pawns could become objects of attack. However, for this it is necessary to radically change the conditions of the struggle on the king's flank. The fact of the matter is that Black's weaknesses are for the present reliably defended, it is not easy to take control of the g and e-files; the position of the
zh: 黑方王的地位被严重削弱，f6、f7和h7兵可能成为攻击对象。然而，为此有必要从根本上改变王翼上的斗争条件。事实上，黑方的弱点目前已被可靠防守，控制g和e线并不容易；的位置

text: White king is also far from being perfect, and, if White, in the course of his attack, has to push the pawns on the king's flank, then all the pre-requisites are there for a counter-attack by the opponent.
zh: 白王也远非完美，如果白在进攻过程中必须将王翼上的兵推下去，那么对手反击的先决条件就具备了。

text: In short, the advantage is on White's side, but to convert it into something real proves to be a complicated and difficult task. In fact, from the further course of the game it is seen that the plan contemplated by Alekhine represents a 40 move process of manoeuvering, in the course of which only one pawn exchange will be made. It is interesting that, in the final manoeuvering, White announces mate in six moves, with the same pieces present as when the process began.
zh: 简而言之，优势在白方这边，但要将其转化为现实，却是一项复杂而艰巨的任务。事实上，从对局的进一步进程可以看出，阿廖欣所设想的方案代表了调动的40步过程，在此过程中只会进行一次兵交换。有趣的是，在最后的调动中，怀特宣布六步杀，并与过程开始时相同的棋子出现。

text: White's plan consists of: (1) the transfer of the king to a safe place on the queen's flank; (2) the storming advance of the g-pawn; and (3) piece manoeuvres with the aim of a harmonious concentration of all his forces and a directing of their co-ordinated blows on the f6 and h7 points.
zh: 白方的计划包括：（1）将王转移到后翼上的安全地点；(2) 猛攻冲兵；（3）棋子运子，其目的是和谐地集中所有力量，并指挥他们对f6和h7点进行协调打击。

text: It is perfectly clear that, with full equality of forces for the attacking and defending sides and a pawn chain position which is not locked, the fulfilment of such a manoeuvering plan looks like being an unusually complex matter.
zh: 很显然，在攻守双方兵力完全平等且兵链阵地未锁定的情况下，完成这样一个调动计划看起来是一件异常复杂的事情。

text: 21. Bc2 Reg8 22. g3 Qd7
zh: 21. Bc2 Reg8 22. g3 Qd7

text: Black manoeuvres without any particular aim. This is easy to understand: there are no weak spots in the enemy position which might allow him to undertake an enterprising operation; at the same time, White's plan is still not clear, indeed he also still cannot create any dangerous threats. One can surmise that, at the present moment, Yates considered his position to be more than reliable.
zh: 黑方运子，没有任何特定目的。这很容易理解：敌方阵地中没有可以进行进攻的薄弱环节；与此同时，怀特的计划仍然不明确，事实上他也仍然无法制造出任何危险的威胁。可以推测，目前，耶茨认为他的立场非常可靠。

text: 23. Rf2 Qe7 24. Kf1
zh: 23. Rf2 Qe7 24. Kf1

text: The king begins a distant journey, which is completed only after 15 moves.
zh: 王开始了一段遥远的旅程，需要15步才能完成。

text: 24 ... Rd8 25. Rd2 b6 26. Qd5 Rgg8 27. Qf5 a5 28. Ke1 Qe6 29 Qh5. Qe7
zh: 24 ... Rd8 25. Rd2 b6 26. Qd5 Rgg8 27. Qf5 a5 28. Ke1 Qe6 29 Qh5. Qe7

text: Black considers that his position is solid and waits while White also convinces himself of this. Therefore his piece manoeuvres do not have any concrete formation, except one thing - they do not worsen his position.
zh: 黑方认为自己的立场稳固并等待，而白方也确信这一点。因此他的棋子运子没有任何具体的阵型，除了一件事——它们不会恶化他的地位。

text: This is the picture that emerges: White purposefully manoeuvres and according to plan, preparing a decisive attack on the king's flank while Black occupies himself for the time being with waiting manoeuvres. It is clear that creative technique, characterised by concrete ideas and purposefulness, must gain victory over passive waiting tactics.
zh: 出现的画面是这样的：白方有目的地运子并按照计划，准备对王翼进行决定性的攻击，而黑方则暂时等待运子。显然，以具体想法和目的为特征的创造性技术必须战胜被动等待策略。

text: 30. Kd1 Rg7 31. Kc1 Nf8 32. Bf5 Re8 33. g4
zh: 30. Kd1 Rg7 31. Kc1 Nf8 32. Bf5 Re8 33. g4

text: Only after 12 moves is this pawn advanced to its appointed square not until the White king is finally "established" in a safe little nook and his pieces are regrouped to extract as much as possible from the advance g4-g5. All this requires scrupulous, thorough work and, of course, patience.
zh: 只有在 12 步之后，这个冲兵才会到达其指定的格，直到白方王最终“建立”在一个安全的小角落，并且他的棋子重新组合以从前进 g4-g5 中提取尽可能多的资金。所有这一切都需要一丝不苟、彻底的工作，当然还需要耐心。

text: Alekhine was a master of great creative dynamism, but dynamics combine badly with such slow manoeuvring. It is all the more interesting to observe that "pathos for patience" with which Alekhine, curbing his temperament and dynamism of thought, carries out the process of many moves of manoeuvring.
zh: 阿廖欣是一位具有巨大创造性活力的大师，但活力与如此缓慢的调动结合得很糟糕。更有趣的是，观察阿廖欣的“耐心的悲伤”，抑制了他的性情和思想活力，执行了调动的许多动作的过程。

text: The piece manoeuvres are instructive and, in order to understand some of them, it is necessary to try to deeply grasp all the ramifications of White's plan. Here, for example, the manoeuvres of the bishop (beginning from the 21st move and going on until
zh: 棋子运子很有启发性，为了理解其中的一些，有必要尝试深入掌握怀特计划的所有后果。这里，例如，象的运子（从第21步开始一直持续到

text: the end of the game): Bf5-c2-f5-
zh: 对局结束）：Bf5-c2-f5-

text: c2-a4-d1-c2-f5. The bishop goes to the c3 and f5 squares three times and to the a4 and d1 squares once. This "running about" might show itself to be pointless and, of course, it does not prove decisive in White's manoeuvring, but it points to the fact that Alekhine, at this time, banished hurry, haste and striving to force the game from his creative methods and devices.
zh: c2-a4-d1-c2-f5。象转至 c3 和 f5 格 3 次，转至 a4 和 d1 格一次。这种“跑来跑去”可能会显得毫无意义，当然，它在怀特的调动中并没有被证明是决定性的，但它指出了这样一个事实：阿廖欣在这个时候，从他的创造性方法和设备中消除了匆忙、仓促和努力来迫使对局。

text: 33 ... Ng6 34. a3 Qd8 35. Bc2 Qc8 36. Kb1 Ne7 37. h3 Ng6 38 Qh6. Qd8 39. Ka2 Ne7
zh: 33 ... Ng6 34. a3 Qd8 35. Bc2 Qc8 36. Kb1 Ne7 37. h3 Ng6 38 Qh6. Qd8 39. Ka2 Ne7

text: So as to reply to 40 Qxf6? with
zh: 以便回复 40 Qxf6?

text: An intermediate move, pursuing the aim of either breaking the harmonious co-operation of the Black rooks, or freeing the e-file from excessive influence of the opponent's forces.
zh: 一个过渡着，追求的目标是要么打破黑方车的和谐合作，要么将e线从对手势力的过度影响中解放出来。

text: 41 ... Reg8 42. Bd1 Qe7 43. Bc2 Nf8 44. Rd5 Ng6 45. Rf5
zh: 41 ... Reg8 42. Bd1 Qe7 43. Bc2 Nf8 44. Rd5 Ng6 45. Rf5

text: The Black knight is now pinned down.
zh: 黑方马现在已被固定。

text: At last! And yet, at the present moment, Alekhine is tempted · should he not wait? In any case, apropos t this move, he noted "Possibly it was more accurate to prepare this break by the move 46 h4. However the text is strong enough."
zh: 终于！然而，此时此刻，阿廖欣却被诱惑了·难道他不应该等待吗？无论如何，对于这一步棋，他指出“通过第 46 步 h4 准备这一突破可能更准确。不过，文字足够有力。”

text: Threats begin to emerge, in the first instance f5.
zh: 威胁开始出现，首先是f5。

text: Other moves lose quickly. For example, 47 ... Rgg8 48 f5 Nf8 49
zh: 其他动作很快就会失败。例如，47。。。 Rgg8 48 f5 Nf8 49

text: Rxg8+ Kxg8 50. f6 or 47 ... Reg8 48. f5 f6 49. Rxg6. 48. Rh5 If now 48. f5, then 48 ... Ne5 49 f6. Rg6! 50. Qxf8+ Rxf8 51. Bxg6
zh: Rxg8+ Kxg8 50. f6 或 47。。。 Reg8 48. f5 f6 49. Rxg6。48. Rh5 如果现在 48. f5，则 48。。。 Ne5 49 f6。Rg6! 50. Qxf8+ Rxf8 51. Bxg6

text: fxg6 and White has only minimal chances of victory.
zh: fxg6 并且白方获胜的机会很小。

text: The manoeuvring enters the final phase. In order to increase the pressure White has to introduce the inactive rook c3 into the fray. This is the next thing he strives for.
zh: 调动进入最后阶段。为了增加压力，白方必须将不活跃的车c3引入战斗。这就是他接下来要努力的事情。

text: 50. Qf6 Nd7 51. Qd4
zh: 50. Qf6 Nd7 51. Qd4

text: Threatening both B or Rxh7.
zh: 威胁 B 或 Rxh7。

text: The weakness of f6 and h7 make Black's position indefensible.
zh: f6和h7的弱点使得黑方的局面站不住脚。

text: Ree7
zh: Ree7

text: Clearly bad is 56 ... Rxg2 57
zh: 显然不好的是 56。。。 Rxg2 57

text: Rxh7+ Kg8 58. Qd5+ Ne6 59 Qxg2+ Ng7 60. Qg6 with the
zh: Rxh7+ Kg8 58. Qd5+ Ne6 59 Qxg2+ Ng7 60. Qg6 与

text: irresistible threat of Rh8+ and Qh7 mate.
zh: Rh8+ 和 Qh7 伴侣的不可抗拒的威胁。

text: Also possible is at once 57 Rh6
zh: 也可能一次 57 Rh6

text: Rxg2 58. Rxf6. 57 ... a4 58. Rh6 Rgf7 59. Rgg6 Nb3 60. Qc3 d5
zh: Rxg2 58. Rxf6. 57 ... a4 58. Rh6 Rgf7 59. Rgg6 Nb3 60. Qc3 d5

text: White announced mate in six moves (63 Rxh7+!).
zh: 白方宣布六步杀 (63 Rxh7+!)。

text: Thus ends the process of 40 moves of manoeuvring. The active side in this process was White. Black, however, stuck to waiting tactics and in the end was mated.
zh: 至此，调动40步的过程结束。这个过程中主动的一方是白方。然而，黑方坚持等待策略，最终被配对。

text: On the examples of classic chess works of Chigorin and Alekhine, we are able to convince ourselves that manoeuvring can conceal profound aims and ideas. However, in order to transform the monotonous process of manoeuvring into a brilliant boon of ideas, it is necessary to combine, in one go, indomitable spirit of struggle, creative inspiration and chess mastery.
zh: 以齐果林和阿廖欣的经典国际象棋作品为例，我们能够说服自己，调动可以隐藏深刻的目的和思想。然而，要将调动单调的过程转化为灿烂的思想恩赐，需要将顽强的奋斗精神、创造性的灵感和棋艺融为一体。

text: If these conditions are absent, then we come witness to manoeuvring which is tiresome, not very interesting and undoubtedly impoverished of the creative content of the chess struggle.
zh: 如果这些条件不存在，那么我们就会看到调动，这是令人厌烦的，不是很有趣，而且无疑缺乏国际象棋斗争的创造性内容。

text: To a certain extent, this is true in respect of the following two illustrations, in which the manoeuvring is half-forced and only half-waiting.
zh: 从某种程度上来说，下面两个例子也是如此，其中调动是一半被迫，一半等待。

text: Despite White's extra pawn in the game Blackburne-Albin from Hastings 1895, he cannot achieve anything - the construction of the position excludes the possibility of a breakthrough. The potential weakness of the Black b6 pawn cannot be realised. There are no open files on the board, and the heavy pieces of both partners are doomed to inactivity. However, having an extra pawn, Blackburne did not want to content himself with a draw. As a result, there arises the process of many moves of manoeuvring, in which White only waits to see if Black will by chance relax his attention to the b6 pawn. Black likewise cannot do anything and is obliged to manoeuvre. The defence of the b6 pawn does not present any particular difficulty. Let us see how events developed.
zh: 尽管怀特在1895年哈斯廷斯布莱克本-阿尔宾的对局中额外兵，但他无法取得任何成果——阵地的构建排除了突破的可能性。黑方 b6 兵的潜在弱点无法被认识到。董事会上没有开放线，双方的重子注定不活跃。然而，拥有额外的兵，布莱克本并不想满足于平局。结果，出现了调动的许多走法过程，其中白方只是等待黑方是否会偶然放松对b6兵的注意力。黑方同样无能为力，必须运子。b6 兵的防御并不存在任何特别的困难。让我们看看事件是如何发展的。

text: Spanish Game
zh: 西班牙开局

text: White: P.Romanovsky
zh: 白方：P.罗曼诺夫斯基

text: Black: M.Botvinnik
zh: 黑方：M.鲍特维尼克

text: (Moscow 1935)
1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4 Bxc6. dxc6 5. Nc3 f6 6. d3
zh: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 Nc6 3. Bb5 a6 4 Bxc6. dxc6 5. Nc3 f6 6. d3

text: A continuation which gives the game a locked character. The struggle now enters a manoeuvring phase which lasts not more, not less than 30 moves. Throughout this long period, the sides 'succeed" in producing just one pawn exchange. Such a process of manoeuvring requires great patience from the partners. In the end it exhausts White, that is the side whose fault it was that the struggle went into manoeuvring channels. "Those who live by the sword, must die by the sword'".
zh: 一个后续手段给对局一个锁定的角色。战斗现在进入调动阶段，持续不少于30步。在这漫长的时间里，双方“成功”只进行了一次兵交换。这样的调动过程需要伙伴们极大的耐心。最终它耗尽了白方的力量，正是白方的过错导致斗争进入了调动通道。“靠剑生者，必死于剑”。

text: Was White forced into his last move? Of course not. It was possible to play 6 d4 exd4 7 Qxd4 Qxd4 8 Nxd4, and the position would assume an open character. However, an early exchange of queens is not to everyone's taste. But the main thing is this, that White reckons on carrying out, in the near future, the advance d3-d4 or f2-f4, opening the centre, but does not take into account that the opponent will prevent the execution of this plan, after which he has to manoeuvre until the end of the game.
zh: 白方是被迫下最后一步的吗？当然不是。可以玩 6 d4 exd4 7 Qxd4 Qxd4 8 Nxd4，并且该位置将假定为空字符。然而，早期交换后并不符合所有人的口味。但最主要的是，白方预计在不久的将来执行d3-d4或f2-f4前进，打开中心，但没有考虑到对手会阻止该计划的执行，之后他必须运子直到对局结束。

text: Ng3
zh: Ng3

text: White reconciles himself to the need for manoeuvring. His last move arms him against Black's possible advance ... f5. Then the e4 point would pass into White's hands and on it he could handily place one of his knights.
zh: 怀特同意自己需要调动。他的最后一步棋使他能够对抗黑方可能的前进……f5。然后e4点将传递到怀特手中，他可以轻松地在其上放置他的马之一。

text: 9 ... Be6 10. c3 Qd7 11. O-O O-O 12. Qc2 Nc6 13. Nd2 Rad8 14 Rad1. b6 15. f3
zh: 9 ... Be6 10. c3 Qd7 11. O-O O-O 12. Qc2 Nc6 13. Nd2 Rad8 14 Rad1. b6 15. f3

text: The advance d4 is prevented, therefore the weakness of the d3 pawn, located on the d-file where Black's heavy pieces dominate, is quite real. The best testimony to this is the fact that it is impossible now for White to play 15 f4, which, after the exchange on f4, leads to the loss of the central pawn. As a result, White is forced into waiting, though 1also not pointless, manoeuvring. As already pointed out, he concentrates his influence in good time on the e4 point, in anticipation of the move ... f5. It is interesting t that even after this the struggle retains a manoeuvring character.
zh: 前进d4被阻止，因此位于d线黑方重子占主导地位的d3兵的弱点是相当真实的。最好的证明就是现在白方不可能下15f4，在f4交换之后，导致中央兵的损失。结果，白方被迫等待，尽管1也并非毫无意义，调动。正如已经指出的，他及时将其影响力集中在e4点上，以预期移动。。。。。。f5。有趣的是，即使在此之后，斗争仍然保留着调动特征。

text: 15 ... Be7 16. Nb3 a5 17 Ncl Bd6 18. Qf2 Ne7 19. Rd2 f5
zh: 15。。。 Be7 16. Nb3 a5 17 Ncl Bd6 18. Qf2 Ne7 19. Rd2 f5

text: Risky, but there was apparently no other way to liven up the struggle. Black thinks the initiative is on his side but, other than by advancing the f-pawn, he cannot show it. Now a light shines before White in the shape of the isolated Black pawn on e5 and a dominating outpost in the centre - the e4 point.
zh: 虽然有风险，但显然没有其他办法可以让斗争变得活跃起来。黑方认为主动权站在他这边，但除了推进 f-兵之外，他无法表现出来。现在，一道光以 e5 上孤立的黑方兵的形状照射在白方面前，并在中心 - e4 点上占据主导地位。

zh: 20. exf5 Nxf5 21. Ne4

text: Here White, tired out from the tortuous and, in the present case, not very creative process s of manoeuvring, overlooked the loss of a pawn after 37 Ne3 and in the end suffered defeat. He should play
zh: 在这里，白方因调动的曲折且在目前情况下不是很有创意的过程而疲惫不堪，忽视了37Ne3后失去兵，最终遭受失败。他应该玩

text: The creative process of chess art suffers particularly when manoeuvring turns out to be a form of voluntary waiting, inactivity, and at times also a refusal to fight.
zh: 当调动被证明是一种自愿等待、不活动，有时甚至是拒绝战斗时，国际象棋艺术的创作过程尤其会受到影响。

text: And though in the practice of our grandmasters and masters, who present themselves before the whole chess world as players with a fighting, energetic, ， enterprising style, such cases are comparatively we nevertheless give one rare, example of this in the hope that it will not be imitated by the readers of this book.
zh: 尽管在我们的特级大师和大师们的实践中，他们以战斗、精力充沛、进取的风格展现在整个国际象棋棋手面前，这样的例子相对较少，但我们还是举一个罕见的例子，希望本书的读者不会效仿。

text: Caro-Kann Defence
zh: 卡罗-康防御

text: White: Y.Averbakh
zh: 白方：Y.阿韦尔巴赫

text: Black: T.Petrosian
zh: 黑方：T.彼得罗相

text: (19th USSR Championship 1951)
zh: （1951年第19届苏联锦标赛）

text: 1. e4 c6 2. Nc3 d5 3. Nf3 Bg4 4 h3. Bxf3 5. Qxf3 Nf6 6. d3 e6
zh: 1. e4 c6 2. Nc3 d5 3. Nf3 Bg4 4 h3. Bxf3 5. Qxf3 Nf6 6. d3 e6

text: The game begins to take on a locked character - the first prerequisite for t transferring it to manoeuvring channels.
zh: 对局开始呈现锁定角色 - 将其转移到调动通道的首要先决条件。

text: Very slow, though repeatedly met in practice. 7 Be2 was played in the first game of the Smyslov. Botvinnik return match, but also upon this the game continuation comes to assume the aspect of a manoeuvring struggle without exchanges.
zh: 非常慢，虽然在实践中多次遇到。7 Be2 在斯梅斯洛夫的第一场对局中进行。鲍特维尼克回归对局，但在此基础上，对局后续手段开始呈现出调动没有交流的斗争的一面。

text: 7 ... Be7 8. Bg2 O-O 9. O-O Na6 10 Qe2. Ne8 11. e5
zh: 7 ... Be7 8. Bg2 O-O 9. O-O Na6 10 Qe2. Ne8 11. e5

text: The present moment in the game is highly instructive. It shows that the process of manoeuvring is far from always created by chance or comes about by coincidence, without depending on the will of the players. Manoeuvring arises at times also as a result of a conscious striving for it by one or both opponents. From the creative point of view, what is not brought about by such striving cannot justify itself.
zh: 对局中的当前时刻非常有启发性。这表明调动的过程并不总是偶然产生或巧合的，而不取决于玩家的意志。调动有时也会由于一个或两个对手有意识地努力而出现。从创造性的角度来看，没有这种努力所带来的东西是不能自圆其说的。

text: Instead of locking the position and automatically y transferring to manoeuvring, White had at his disposal an active plan of attack in the centre: 11 d4 followed by Be3, Rad1, and f4. Black could hardly accept the pawn sacrifice 11 ..
zh: 白方并没有锁定位置并自动转移到调动，而是在中心制定了一个主动攻击计划：11d4，然后是Be3、Rad1和f4。黑方很难接受兵弃子 11。。

text: dxe4 12. Nxe4! Qxd4, then 13. Rd1
zh: dxe4 12. Nxe4! Qxd4，然后 13. Rd1

text: Qb6 14 Rd7 Bf6 15 c3 and White threatens, after Be3, not only to recover the pawn but also to obtain a positional superiority.
zh: Qb6 14 Rd7 Bf6 15 c3 并且白方威胁，在Be3之后，不仅要收回兵，还要获得位置优势。

text: If the exchange exf6 suits Black, then why did he not play 14 ... f6?
zh: 如果交换 exf6 适合黑，那么他为什么不下 14。。。 f6?

text: 15. Bf4 Rb8 16. Rc1 Na6 17. cxd5
zh: 15. Bf4 Rb8 16. Rc1 Na6 17. cxd5

text: cxd5 The last exchange in this game!
zh: cxd5本场对局最后一次交流！

text: White wrongly refrains from the manoeuvre Nc3-b1-d2-b3, which gives him chances of seizing the initiative. Something like this might 0ccur: 18 Nc3 Nec7 19 Nb1
zh: 白方错误地放弃了运子Nc3-b1-d2-b3，这给了他抓住主动权的机会。像这样的事情可能会 0ccur： 18 Nc3 Nec7 19 Nb1

zh: Rfc8 20. Nd2 b4 21. Nb3 Nb5 22 Be3. Rxc1 23. Rxc1 Rc8 24. Rxc8+ Qxc8 25. d4 Qc6 26. Bf1 Nac7 27

zh: h5，然后g4，为白方平方象打开动作格。

text: He gets nothing out of this. Possible is 21 h5 h6 22 Bf3, and then Kh2, Rg1 and g4, but White continues to manoeuvre.
zh: 他从中一无所获。可能的是 21 h5 h6 22 Bf3，然后是 Kh2、Rg1 和 g4，但白方继续运子。

text: 21 ... Bf8 22. Bh3 Qf7 23. Rfd1 Qe8 24. Bf1 a5 25. Be3 a4 26 Qe1. Nc6 27. Ne2 Nb4 28. Nc3
zh: 21 ... Bf8 22. Bh3 Qf7 23. Rfd1 Qe8 24. Bf1 a5 25. Be3 a4 26 Qe1. Nc6 27. Ne2 Nb4 28. Nc3

text: Nc6 29 Ne2 Nb4 Draw agreed!
zh: Nc6 29 Ne2 Nb4 抽签同意！

text: The chess struggle, which is full of initiative and enterprising play, assumes quite a different character.
zh: 充满主动权和进取心的国际象棋斗争呈现出截然不同的特征。

text: We have already used the term "initiative" time and again in the pages of this book. The Latin word "initium"1 means the principle of initiative. Initiative in life - this is a display of activity in any area of man's work. The initiative is born, becomes apparent and is developed out of a resolute striving for individual or collective thoughts. In the chess struggle the initiative likewise presents itself as a resolute activity, directed towards the creation of immediate threats to the opponent, to the constraint of his position, to the restriction of the mobility of his forces s and his possibilities in general.
zh: 我们已经在本书中多次使用了术语“主动权”。拉丁词“initium”1 的意思是主动权的原理。生活中的主动权 - 这是人类工作任何领域活动的展示。主动权是在个人或集体思想的坚定努力中诞生、变得明显并发展起来的。在国际象棋斗争中，主动权同样表现为一种坚决的活动，旨在对对手产生直接威胁，限制他的位置，限制他的力量的机动性和总体可能性。

text: More often than not in the chess game, one of the opponents holds the initiative, but there will be occasions when the initiative runs across a counter-initiative, particularly when attacks are conducted on opposite flanks. The initiative will quite often bear a temporary character: it either runs dry or is intercepted by the opposing side.
zh: 在国际象棋对局中，对手之一经常持有主动权，但有时主动权会碰到对手主动权，特别是在对侧进行攻击时。主动权通常会具有先手的稀有特征：它要么耗尽，要么被对方拦截。

text: From the point of view of scale, manifestation of the initiative can be divided into several categories. The initiative can be small, firm, durable, dangerous, s strong etc. Sometimes it is said that the initiative develops into an attack. This is an inaccuracy. An attack represents an offensive. The initiative likewise often attends threats and offensives. But if an attack is always an initiative, then an initiative cannot in all cases be identified with an attack. For example, in the game Alekhine- Yates, White held the initiative for 40 moves - the whole process of manoeuvring - but he only obtained an attack at the end of the game, after the move g5, when he began an assault on the f6 and h7 pawns and created mating threats. Therefore to say that the initiative turns into an attack is roughly the same as talking about the change of boldness into bravery, cowardice into timidity, a laugh into a roar, etc.
zh: 从规模上来看，主动权的表现形式可以分为几类。主动权可以是小、坚固、耐用、危险、强大等。有时据说主动权发展成一种攻击。这是不准确的。攻击就代表进攻。主动权同样经常参与威胁和攻击。但如果攻击始终是主动权，则主动权无法在所有情况下都被识别为攻击。例如，在阿廖欣-耶茨对局中，白方持有主动权40步——调动的整个过程——但他只在对局结束时获得一次攻击，在g5步之后，当他开始攻击f6和h7时兵并创建了将杀威胁。所以说主动权变成攻击，大致相当于说大胆变成勇敢，怯懦变成胆怯，笑变成吼等等。

text: In the opening of the game, White holds a small initiative thanks to the right of the first move (let us say, after 1 d4, Black is deprived of the reply 1 ... e5). If Black succeeds in neutralising even such a slight initiative in the opening, then it is customary to consider that he has equalised the game, though, in the present case, the term "equalisation" bears a particularly conditional character.
zh: 在对局的开局中，由于第一步的权利，白方持有一个小主动权（比方说，在1 d4之后，黑方被剥夺了回复1。。。 e5）。如果黑方在开局中成功地抵消了哪怕如此轻微的主动权，那么通常会认为他已经扳平了对局，尽管在目前的情况下，“扳平”一词带有特别的条件特征。

text: It happens that an opening develops symmetrically. ． This is observed sometimes in the Four Knights Opening, in the exchange variation of the French Defence, in the Italian Game and even in the Queen's Gambit. More often than not, White succeeds in obtaining a small initiative in symmetrical systems, once again thanks to having the first move.
zh: 碰巧开口是对称形成的。．有时会在四马开局、法兰西防御的兑换变例、意大利对局甚至后翼弃兵中观察到这种情况。通常情况下，白方会在对称系统中成功获得小主动权，这再次归功于先手棋。

text: Seizing the initiative is a definite creative achievement. The extent of this advantage depends on the character and strength of the initiative.
zh: 抓住主动权绝对是一项创造性成就。这种优势的程度取决于主动权的性格和强度。

text: Without mentioning the purely chess advantages of holding the initiative, one can boldly maintain that it evokes creative enthusiasm, stimulates an increase in work-rate of thought and imagination, promotes confidence in one's own strength. On the other hand, the need to parry the opponent's initiative quite often has a disastrous psychological influence, having a negative effect on the quality of play, on thes steadfastness of defence, and at times leads to demoralisation. It is no coincidence that a sizeable proportion of mistakes and oversights fall to the lot of chessplayers who come under the influence of the opponent's initiative in a game.
zh: 且不说持有主动权纯粹的国际象棋优势，我们可以大胆地认为它能唤起创造热情，激发思维和想象力工作效率的提高，增强对自身实力的信心。另一方面，招架对手主动权的需要常常会产生灾难性的心理影响，对对局质量、防守稳定性产生负面影响，有时还会导致士气低落。相当大比例的错误和疏忽都是由在对局中受到对手主动权影响的棋手造成的，这并非巧合。

text: The following two games might serve as a good illustration of this statement.
zh: 下面的两场对局或许可以很好地说明这一点。

text: An interesting game in which the role of the initiative was expressed very boldly. For the first ten moves, White held quite firmly a small opening initiative. It waned after 12 e3, and finally ran dry after 16 Be2. From this moment Black directed the struggle towards a capture of the initiative. He succeeded in accomplishing this as a result of White's mistake on the 23rd move.
zh: 一个有趣的对局，其中主动权的角色表现得非常大胆。在前十步棋中，白方相当牢固地占据了一个小开口主动权。它在 12 点 e3 后减弱，并最终在 16 点 Be2 后枯竭。从这一刻起，黑方将斗争方向转向夺取主动权。由于白方在第 23 步棋的失误，他成功地完成了这一任务。

text: Black's initiative increased to a "crescendo" and quickly reached the force of a decisive attack, which already after eight moves achieved its objective. Mention should be made of the exceptional harmony yin the final attacking operation of all Black's pieces.
zh: 黑方主动权上升到“渐强”，很快就达到了决定性进攻的力度，八步后就达到了目的。值得一提的是全黑棋子最后进攻行动中的异常和谐。

text: The initiative - this is a symbol of creative life in chess. The initiative - is an enemy of passivity and inactivity, waiting manoeuvring and complacent contemplation. This is why, in each period of the chess struggle, defending Or attacking, parrying or delivering blows, in moments of difficult trials and triumphant ideas, we ought to remember that the unfailing slogan, always and everywhere accompanying our inspired and creative thoughts, must be the slogan: "The desire for the initiative!".
zh: 主动权 - 这是国际象棋中创造性生活的象征。主动权 - 是被动和不活动、等待调动和自满沉思的敌人。这就是为什么，在国际象棋斗争的每一个时期，无论是防守还是进攻，是招架还是打击，在艰难的考验和胜利的思想时刻，我们都应该记住，始终随处伴随着我们的灵感和创造性思维的永恒口号一定是：“对主动权的渴望！”。

text: The Two Bishops
zh: 双象

text: It is generally well-known that the relative strength of the pieces is a variable value which can both increase or decrease depending on the arrangement of other pieces and the dynamics of the position.
zh: 众所周知，棋子的相对强度是一个可变值，它可以根据其他棋子的排列和位置的动态而增加或减少。

text: The rook and bishop on open lines, the knight established on a weak square - all these factors increase the power of piece activity. The "eternal" knight is such a threatening force that, for the most part, it is equivalent to an extra exchange for the opponent. The unfailing question of amateurs as to which is the stronger - knight or bishop, is met by the stereotyped reply: in one position the bishop is stronger, in another - the knight. It all depends s on what pawn material is on the board, what is its structure and what positions, in the first instance, the pieces, comparative in strength, are occupying. It goes without saying, the position of the other pieces must likewise be taken into account.
zh: 开放线路上的车和象，建立在弱格上的马 - 所有这些因素都增加了子力活动的能力。“永恒”马是一种具有如此威胁性的力量，在很大程度上，它相当于给对手额外的交换。业余爱好者总是会问马或象哪个更强，但得到了刻板的回答：在一个位置上象更强，在另一个位置上 - 马。这一切都取决于板上的兵材料、其结构是什么以及首先，相对强度的棋子占据什么位置。不言而喻，另一个棋子的位置也必须同样考虑在内。

text: Among those pieces whose strength increases appreciably depending on the features of the position and the harmony of activity, the two bishops have attracted particular attention since the beginning of the century.
zh: 在这些棋子中，其力量根据位置特征和活动的和谐程度而明显增加，双象自本世纪初以来特别受到关注。

text: In a number of games, according to the positional conditions, the two bishops were able to show themselves as a threatening force, exceeding the power of two other minor pieces and sometimes even a rook and minor piece.
zh: 在多场对局中，根据位置条件，双象能够展现出自己的威胁力量，超过另外两个轻子，有时甚至超过车和轻子。

text: Steinitz, the founder-teacher of positional play, seemed to be carried away with the effectiveness of the harmonious activity of the two bishops and called this "the advantage of the two bishops". The two bishops figure here, as also in many other evaluations, as an abstract positional factor, embodying one aspect of the advantage.
zh: 局面型下法的创始人兼教师斯坦尼茨似乎对双象和谐活动的有效性着迷，并称其为“双象的优势”。这里的双象数字，以及许多其他评估中的一样，作为一个抽象的位置因素，体现了优势的一个方面。

text: The first to come out decisively against this view was Chigorin. He expounded his views on this question very thoroughly in polemics with Em.Lasker, when the world champion's book Common Sense in Chess was published in 1896. Lasker gave this bold name to a collection of twelve lectures which he had given before an audience of London chessplayers. There is no place here to assess the merits and demerits of this work which, though pretentious, undoubtedly deserves attention. However, we recall it solely in connection with one position, on account of which arose a dispute between Chigorin and Lasker on the question which interests us about the two bishops.
zh: 第一个坚决反对这种观点的是齐果林。当世界冠军的书《国际象棋常识》于 1896 年出版时，他在与拉斯克的争论中非常彻底地阐述了他对这个问题的看法。 拉斯克为他在伦敦棋手观众面前发表的十二个演讲集起了这个大胆的名字。这里没有地方评估这部作品的优点和缺点，尽管它自命不凡，但无疑值得关注。然而，我们只记得它与一个立场有关，由于该立场，齐果林和拉斯克之间就我们对双象感兴趣的问题产生了争议。

text: In the fourth lecture, Lasker chose as the subject of his talk, the opening theme - the Evans Gambit. In particular, he presented the following variation: 1 e4 e5 2 Nf3
zh: 在第四堂课中，拉斯克选择了开场主题——埃文斯策略作为演讲主题。他特别提出了以下变体： 1 e4 e5 2 Nf3

text: Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 Bxb4 5. c3 Ba5 6. d4 d6 7. O-O Bb6 8. dxe5 dxe5 9 Qb3. Qf6 10. Bd5 Nge7 11. Bg5 Qg6 12. Bxe7 Kxe7 13. Bxc6 Qxc6 14 Nxe5. Qe6 15. Qa3+.
zh: Nc6 3. Bc4 Bc5 4. b4 Bxb4 5. c3 Ba5 6. d4 d6 7. O-O Bb6 8. dxe5 dxe5 9 Qb3. Qf6 10. Bd5 Nge7 11. Bg5 Qg6 12. Bxe7 Kxe7 13. Bxc6 Qxc6 14 Nxe5. Qe6 15. Qa3+.

text: Lasker estimated this position, after the possible replies 15 ... Kf6 or 15 5 ... c5, in Black's favour, since he has, in his own words, two bishops, excellent development of forces and a strong position.
zh: 拉斯克在可能的答复 15。。。 Kf6 或 15 5。。。 c5 后估计了这个位置，对黑方有利，因为用他自己的话说，他拥有双象出色的力量发展和强大的地位。

text: We give Chigorin's objection to this assessment which appeared on 30January 1897 in the（ chess column of the newspaper Novoe Vremya: "By indicating the two bishops, Herr Lasker naturally gives the understanding that the two bishops are superior in strength to the two knights. Consequently, taking into account also the excellent development of forces and the "strong" position, the Black player has a significant advantage over the opponent and every chance of victory. However, the assessment of the position, made by Herr Lasker, in my opinion is totally subjective eand hardly proves to be correct in practice. He e not only does not confirm this, even if only with a superficial analysis of the position, but also explains nothing to the amateur who is interested more in the question: in what way can the two bishops show their "strength" over two knights in the present position, and what role will they play?
zh: 我们对齐果林对这一评估的反对意见发表在1897年1月30日《Novoe Vremya》报纸的国际象棋专栏中：“通过指出双象，拉斯克先生自然地给出了这样的理解：双象在力量上优于两个马。因此，还考虑到力量的出色发展在“强”位置上，黑方对对手有显着的优势，并且有获胜的机会。然而，在我看来，Herr 拉斯克对位置的评估完全是主观的，并且在实践中很难证明是正确的。他不仅没有证实这一点，即使只是对位置进行了肤浅的分析，而且也没有向那些对双象更感兴趣的问题解释什么。在目前的位置上有超过两个马的“力量”，他们将扮演什么角色？

text: It is interesting that the position reached in Herr Lasker's variation can also be obtained in the practical game. Therefore, being personally y interested in it, I endeavoured to investigate it. But my analysis led to a completely opposite conclusion, i.e. that all the advantages in the position are to be found on White's side. It would hardly be a mistake to say that detailed analysis and practice will prove that Black's position is even irreparable.
zh: 有趣的是，Herr 拉斯克的变体所达到的位置也可以在实际对局中获得。因此，出于个人的兴趣，我努力进行调查。但我的分析却得出了完全相反的结论，即局面上的所有优势都在白方这边。可以说，经过详细的分析和实践，黑方的局面甚至是不可挽回的。

zh: 这里有一些变化。拉斯克先生认为，黑方通过在第 15 步下棋。。。 Kf6 或。。。 c5，将拥有他所说的所有优势。当王移动到f6时，白方当然将马撤退到f3。。。在16。。。g6上，白方以双重威胁回复17c4

After 16 .. f617 Nf3 followed by f5,c4 (which Black could only temporarily prevent by retreating with the queen to f7), Nc3-d5, White will undoubtedly find himself in the better position. Upon the move 16 ... Bd7, however, White could immediately deprive Black of that strength, which Herr Lasker sees it as; but it is better for White, in my opinion, to carry out his plan by playing c4, Nc3, etc. On other moves for Black: with the king, queen or one of the pawns, White almost invariably fulfils his plan, as also upon the move 16 .. Rd8, the consequences of which I mainly looked at...

text: As I have already said, White could obtain an excellent position after the moves Nf3 and f5 or Nd2 etc., but I want to present variations in which the strength of the knight on the d5 square becomes clear by visual demonstration.

Qd2 28 Rg1) and White must win.

zh: 白方很可能会成功继续 22f6，但 22Rb3 棋的攻击更为有效。

text: The following variations point to the lack of a defence for Black. From these it becomes clear that both bishops cannot take an active role in the defence of the king against the attack of only one knight:
zh: 以下变化表明黑方缺乏防守。由此可见，两个象不能在防御王中发挥积极作用，以抵御仅一个马的攻击：

zh: (a) 22。。。 Kg8 23. Rh3 Qg5 24 Rg3。Qh6 25. f6 g6 26. Qc3 Be6（如果 26。。。 Qh5，则 27. f7+ Kh8 - 或 27。。。 Kf8 28. Nf6 Qh629. Qxe5 Bc6 30. Rh3 并获胜 - 28. Nf6 Qh6 29. Nxd7 Rxd7 30. Qxe5+ 且

text: Those variations, of course, do not exhaust all the means defence. Black could have put up more resistance by not making the
zh: 当然，这些变化并没有用尽所有防御手段。黑方本可以通过不让棋来进行更多的抵抗
